questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to decorate a Christmas tree safely with electric lights
The history of the Christmas tree tradition in Germany and Britain
How much British families spend on Christmas presents each year
Whether real or fake trees are better, including for the planet
questions.why: Neil and Sam ask what impact real and artificial trees have on the environment.

questions.q: When Neil says Christmas 'comes at a price', what does he mean?
options: Presents are too expensive
It has a cost for the environment
Parties are tiring
Food prices go up at Christmas
questions.why: He says, 'I mean it comes at a cost to the environment.'

questions.q: Why does Phil like having a real tree?
options: It is much cheaper than buying a good fake one
His family grows them on a farm in the country
An evergreen tree in the house has special meaning
It is easier to decorate and smells nice
questions.why: He says trees are symbolic, as something that stays green all year.

questions.q: What makes Roy happy about buying a real tree?
options: When the seller promises to plant two or three more
When the tree is very tall and reaches the ceiling
When the tree is delivered to his home for free
When he can recycle it at the council after Christmas
questions.why: He's happy if he buys from someone who promises to grow two or three in its place.

questions.q: Why does Feifei have a plastic tree?
options: She doesn't like the smell of real trees
It can be used every year, so it saves money
It is better for the environment
Real trees are hard to find where she lives
questions.why: She has reused it for about nine years, so it's more economical.

questions.q: What is Neil's own opinion about Christmas trees?
options: Fake trees are the best choice
People shouldn't have any tree
It doesn't matter which kind you have
Nothing is better than a real tree
questions.why: Neil says, 'you can't beat having a real Christmas tree.'

questions.q: According to BBC Reality Check, what makes a real tree's carbon footprint higher?
options: Being put in landfill after Christmas
Being composted
Growing for 12 years
Taking nitrogen from the soil
questions.why: Sam says if it ends up in landfill, the tree's carbon footprint will be higher.

questions.q: What is said about fake trees?
options: They are usually made locally in small British factories
They are easy to recycle once you no longer want them
They are usually imported and can't normally be recycled
They absorb carbon from the air, just like real trees
questions.why: Neil says a fake tree is usually imported and can't usually be recycled, but can be reused.
